summary: 马铃薯从南美安第斯地区传入欧洲后，一度遭到怀疑。各国推广方式不同，但其高产、易煮的特性最终让它成为重要主食，尤其改变了爱尔兰的食物供应与人口增长。
logic: 西班牙引入与欧洲抵触
王室和政策促使人们尝试
高产作物改变人口格局

paragraphs.brief: 马铃薯在南美洲的起源
sentences: The potato was first cultivated in South America between three and seven thousand years ago, though scientists believe they may have grown wild in the region as long as 13,000 years ago.
约三千至七千年前，南美洲的人们最早开始栽培马铃薯。不过科学家认为，它在当地野生生长的历史可能长达一万三千年。
The genetic patterns of potato distribution indicate that the potato probably originated in the mountainous west-central region of the continent.
土豆分布的遗传模式表明，土豆可能起源于该大陆的中西部山区。
paragraphs.gist: 南美人在三千至七千年前开始种植马铃薯，野生祖先可能更早已在当地生长，遗传分布指向南美洲中西部山区。

paragraphs.brief: 印加人的储粮技术与用途
sentences: Early Spanish chroniclers who misused the Indian word batata (sweet potato) as the name for the potato noted the importance of the tuber to the Incan Empire.
早期西班牙编年史家误用当地词 batata（甘薯）称呼马铃薯，也记下了这种块茎对印加帝国的重要性。

The Incas had learned to preserve the potato for storage by dehydrating and mashing potatoes into a substance called chuño, which could be stored in a room for up to 10 years, providing excellent insurance against possible crop failures.
印加人学会将马铃薯脱水捣碎，做成称为楚纽的食物，可在屋内保存长达十年，为日后可能出现的歉收提供保障。
As well as using the food as a staple crop, the Incas thought potatoes made childbirth easier and used them to treat injuries.
除了作主食，印加人还相信马铃薯有助分娩，并用它处理伤口。
paragraphs.gist: 印加人以马铃薯为主食，把它脱水捣成能存十年的楚纽以防歉收，还相信它有助分娩并可用于处理伤口。

paragraphs.brief: 西班牙征服者初遇马铃薯
sentences: The Spanish conquistadors first encountered the potato when they arrived in Peru in 1532 in search of gold, and noted Inca miners eating chuño.
1532年西班牙征服者到秘鲁寻找黄金，第一次见到了马铃薯，并注意到印加矿工在吃楚纽。

At the time the Spaniards failed to realize that the potato represented a far more important treasure than either silver or gold, but they did gradually begin to use potatoes as basic rations aboard their ships.
西班牙人当时没有意识到马铃薯代表着比银或黄金更重要的宝藏，但他们确实逐渐开始使用马铃薯作为船上的基本口粮。
After the arrival of the potato in Spain in 1570, a few Spanish farmers began to cultivate them on a small scale, mostly as food for livestock.
在马铃薯于1570年抵达西班牙之后，一些西班牙农民开始小规模耕种，主要作为牲畜食品。
paragraphs.gist: 西班牙征服者在秘鲁见到矿工食用楚纽，后来把马铃薯用作船上口粮，约在1570年传入西班牙后才少量种作牲畜饲料。

paragraphs.brief: 欧洲早期的疑惧与偏见
sentences: Throughout Europe, potatoes were regarded with suspicion, distaste and fear.
在整个欧洲，马铃薯受到怀疑、厌恶和恐惧。
Generally considered to be unfit for human consumption, they were used only as animal fodder and sustenance for the starving.
人们普遍认为马铃薯不适合人吃，只把它当牲畜饲料，或给濒临饥饿的人暂时充饥。
In northern Europe, potatoes were primarily grown in botanical gardens as an exotic novelty.
在北欧，土豆主要生长在植物园，作为一种奇特的新奇事物。
Even peasants refused to eat from a plant that produced ugly, misshapen tubers and that had come from a heathen civilization.
就连农民也不愿吃这种来自异教文明、长出丑陋畸形块茎的植物。
Some felt that the potato plant’s resemblance to plants in the nightshade family hinted that it was the creation of witches or devils.
有人觉得马铃薯植株与其他茄科植物相似，仿佛是女巫或魔鬼的造物。
paragraphs.gist: 欧洲人最初常把马铃薯当作饲料、饥荒食品或植物园奇物，块茎的外形、外来背景和与茄科植物相似的特征又加深了疑虑。

sentences: In meat-loving England, farmers and urban workers regarded potatoes with extreme distaste.
在热爱肉类的英格兰，农民和城市工人对土豆的厌恶程度极高。
In 1662, the Royal Society recommended the cultivation of the tuber to the English government and the nation, but this recommendation had little impact.
1662年，皇家学会向英格兰政府和民众推荐种植这种块茎，但反响不大。
Potatoes did not become a staple until, during the food shortages associated with the Revolutionary Wars, the English government began to officially encourage potato cultivation.
直到革命战争引发食品短缺、英国政府正式鼓励种植时，马铃薯才逐渐成为主食。
In 1795, the Board of Agriculture issued a pamphlet entitled “Hints Respecting the Culture and Use of Potatoes”; this was followed shortly by pro-potato editorials and potato recipes in The Times.
1795年农业委员会印发《关于马铃薯栽培与使用的建议》小册子，此后不久《泰晤士报》也刊登了支持种植马铃薯的社论和食谱。
Gradually, the lower classes began to follow the lead of the upper classes.
下层社会逐渐开始仿效上层人士。
paragraphs.gist: 英格兰早期推广马铃薯成效甚微，直到战争引发粮食短缺，政府宣传、报纸食谱和上层阶级示范才带动普及。

paragraphs.brief: 法国王室佩花的示范作用
sentences: A similar pattern emerged across the English Channel in the Netherlands, Belgium and France.
在英吉利海峡另一侧，荷兰、比利时和法国也出现了类似情况。

While the potato slowly gained ground in eastern France (where it was often the only crop remaining after marauding soldiers plundered wheat fields and vineyards), it did not achieve widespread acceptance until the late 1700s.
马铃薯逐渐在法国东部流行，当地麦田和葡萄园遭士兵洗劫后，它往往是唯一留下的作物；但直到18世纪末，它才得到普遍接受。
The peasants remained suspicious, in spite of a 1771 paper from the Faculté de Paris testifying that the potato was not harmful but beneficial.
尽管1771年巴黎学界的一篇论文证明马铃薯无害而且有益，农民们仍然心存疑虑。

The people began to overcome their distaste when the plant received the royal seal of approval: Louis XVI began to sport a potato flower in his buttonhole, and Marie-Antoinette wore a purple potato blossom in her hair.
王室表示认可后，人们才渐渐放下反感：路易十六开始在衣服扣眼佩戴马铃薯花，玛丽·安托瓦内特也在发间别上紫色的马铃薯花。
paragraphs.gist: 法国农民即使见到学术报告仍怀疑马铃薯，直到18世纪末国王与王后佩戴马铃薯花，王室表态才逐渐消除疑虑。

paragraphs.brief: 普鲁士看守薯田的用意
sentences: Frederick the Great of Prussia saw the potato’s potential to help feed his nation and lower the price of bread, but faced the challenge of overcoming the people’s prejudice against the plant.
普鲁士的腓特烈大帝看出马铃薯有助于养活国民、降低面包价格，但他首先要想办法消除民众对这种作物的偏见。

When he issued a 1774 order for his subjects to grow potatoes as protection against famine, the town of Kolberg replied: “The things have neither smell nor taste, not even the dogs will eat them, so what use are they to us?”
1774年他下令臣民种马铃薯以防饥荒，科尔贝格镇回应说：“这东西没有香味也没有滋味，连狗也不吃，对我们有什么用？”

Trying a less direct approach to encourage his subjects to begin planting potatoes, Frederick used a bit of reverse psychology: he planted a royal field of potato plants and stationed a heavy guard to protect this field from thieves.
腓特烈转而利用逆反心理，在王室田地里种下马铃薯，派重兵守卫，防人偷盗。
Nearby peasants naturally assumed that anything worth guarding was worth stealing, and so sneaked into the field and snatched the plants for their home gardens.
附近的农民自然觉得，值得看守的东西一定值得偷，于是悄悄溜进田里，把马铃薯植株带回自家菜园。
Of course, this was entirely in line with Frederick’s wishes.
当然，这完全符合弗雷德里克的愿望。
paragraphs.gist: 普鲁士国王命令种植马铃薯遭拒，便改派重兵看守王室薯田，引得农民认定植株珍贵，反而主动偷回家栽种。

paragraphs.brief: 工业城市里的高产口粮
sentences: Historians debate whether the potato was primarily a cause or an effect of the huge population boom in industrial-era England and Wales.
历史学家争论的是，马铃薯主要是工业时代英格兰和威尔士人口激增的原因，还是这一增长的结果。
Prior to 1800, the English diet had consisted primarily of meat, supplemented by bread, butter and cheese.
1800年以前，英国的饮食主要是肉类，并辅以面包、黄油和奶酪。
Few vegetables were consumed, most vegetables being regarded as nutritionally worthless and potentially harmful.
蔬菜很少被消费，大多数蔬菜被认为在营养上毫无价值，而且可能有害。
This view began to change gradually in the late 1700s.
这种观点在1700年代末开始逐渐改变。

The Industrial Revolution was drawing an ever-increasing percentage of the populace into crowded cities, where only the richest could afford homes with ovens or coal storage rooms, and people were working 12–16-hour days which left them with little time or energy to prepare food.
工业革命吸引越来越多人进入拥挤的城市，那里只有富人才住得起带烤炉或储煤室的房子；人们每天工作12至16小时，几乎没有时间和精力做饭。
High-yielding, easily prepared potato crops were the obvious solution to England’s food problems.
高产、容易烹调的马铃薯，成了英国解决粮食问题的一个显而易见的选择。
paragraphs.gist: 工业化把人们带进住房简陋、工时漫长的城市，高产又易烹调的马铃薯正适合这种生活，也引发它与人口增长孰因孰果的讨论。

paragraphs.brief: 爱尔兰农户主动接受种植
sentences: Whereas most of their neighbours regarded the potato with suspicion and had to be persuaded to use it by the upper classes, the Irish peasantry embraced the tuber more passionately than anyone since the Incas.
邻国的农民多对马铃薯心怀疑虑，要靠上层人士劝说才肯食用，而爱尔兰农民对这种块茎的热爱却是印加人以来少有的。
The potato was well suited to the Irish soil and climate, and its high yield suited the most important concern of most Irish farmers: to feed their families.
土豆非常适合爱尔兰的土壤和气候，其高产量适合大多数爱尔兰农民最重要的关切：养活他们的家庭。
paragraphs.gist: 爱尔兰农民主动接受了适合当地土壤和气候的马铃薯，其高产量正好满足农户养活家人的首要需要。

paragraphs.brief: 马铃薯与爱尔兰人口增长
sentences: The most dramatic example of the potato’s potential to alter population patterns occurred in Ireland, where the potato had become a staple by 1800.
马铃薯有能力改变人口格局，爱尔兰就是最鲜明的例子：到1800年，它已成为当地的主食。

The Irish population doubled to eight million between 1780 and 1841, this without any significant expansion of industry or reform of agricultural techniques beyond the widespread cultivation of the potato.
1780至1841年，爱尔兰人口翻倍至八百万，期间工业并无显著扩张，除普遍种植马铃薯外也未大规模改革农业技术。

Though Irish landholding practices were primitive in comparison with those of England, the potato’s high yields allowed even the poorest farmers to produce more healthy food than they needed with scarcely any investment or hard labour.
虽然爱尔兰的土地占有制度与英格兰相比还很原始，但马铃薯产量很高，连最贫穷的农民也能用极少的投入和劳力，种出超过自身所需的营养食物。
Even children could easily plant, harvest and cook potatoes, which of course required no threshing, curing or grinding.
连孩子也能轻松种植、收获和烹煮马铃薯，因为它无需脱粒、熟化或磨粉。
The abundance provided by potatoes greatly decreased infant mortality and encouraged early marriage.
马铃薯带来的充足粮食大幅降低了婴儿死亡率，也鼓励人们较早结婚。
paragraphs.gist: 马铃薯让爱尔兰贫农以很少劳力取得充足食物，婴儿死亡减少、早婚增加，人口在1780至1841年间翻倍至八百万。

items.en: Early Spanish chroniclers called the potato by the Incan name ‘chuño’.
items.zh: 早期西班牙编年史家用印加名称 chuño 称呼马铃薯。
items.why: 题干说他们用“chufio”来称呼土豆，而原文指出早期西班牙编年史作者误用的是 batata,与题干不符，故为 FALSE。

items.en: The purpose of the Spanish coming to Peru was to find potatoes.
items.zh: 西班牙人来到秘鲁的目的是为了找到土豆。
items.why: 西班牙征服者前往秘鲁是为了寻找黄金，只是在那里第一次遇到马铃薯。

items.en: The Spanish believed that the potato had the same nutrients as other vegetables.
items.zh: 西班牙人认为马铃薯与其他蔬菜具有同样的营养。
items.why: 西班牙编年史作者注意到马铃薯对印加人的重要性，没有将它的营养与其他蔬菜加以比较。

items.en: Peasants at that time did not like to eat potatoes because they were ugly.
items.zh: 当时的农民不喜欢吃马铃薯，因为它的外形难看。
items.why: 题干称农民因土豆“丑陋”而不愿食用，与原文描述一致，故为 TRUE。

items.en: The popularity of potatoes in the UK was due to food shortages during the war.
items.zh: 土豆在联合王国的流行是由于战争期间粮食短缺。
items.why: 英国土豆流行与战时粮食短缺直接相关，题干表述吻合，故为 TRUE。

items.en: In France, people began to overcome their disgust towards potatoes because the King put a potato ________ in his buttonhole.
items.zh: 法国国王在衣服的纽扣眼里别上了马铃薯的________，人们对马铃薯的反感才开始消退。
items.why: 填入体现法国人开始克服厌恶的关键“flower”。

items.en: Frederick realised the potential of the potato, but he had to handle the ________ from ordinary people.
items.zh: 腓特烈看到了马铃薯的潜力，但他必须应对普通民众的________。
items.why: 普鲁士国王需应对民众的“prejudice”。

items.en: The King of Prussia adopted a form of ________ psychology to make people accept potatoes.
items.zh: 普鲁士国王利用一种________心理，让人们接受马铃薯。
items.why: 回到对应内容“腓特烈转而利用逆反心理，在王室田地里种下马铃薯，派重兵守卫，防人偷盗”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Before 1800, English people preferred eating ________ with bread, butter and cheese.
items.zh: 1800年以前，英格兰人更喜欢把________配着面包、黄油和奶酪吃。
items.why: 1800 年前英国人偏好吃的是 meat。

items.en: The obvious way to deal with England’s food problems was high-yielding potato ________.
items.zh: 解决英格兰粮食问题的一个显而易见的办法，是种植高产的马铃薯________。
items.why: 高产的 potato “crops”是解决方案，填 crops.

items.en: The Irish ________ and climate suited potatoes well.
items.zh: 爱尔兰的________和气候都很适合种马铃薯。

items.en: Between 1780 and 1841, thanks to the ________ of the potato, the Irish population doubled to eight million.
items.zh: 1780年至1841年间，得益于马铃薯的________，爱尔兰人口翻了一番，达到八百万。
items.why: 因土豆的广泛“cultivation”而人口翻倍，填 cultivation。

items.en: The potato’s high yields helped the poorest farmers to produce more healthy food almost without ________.
items.zh: 得益于马铃薯的高产，即使最贫穷的农民也几乎无须任何________，便能生产更多有益健康的食物。
items.why: 高产让贫困农民几乎不需“investment”,填investment。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 第 2 段 · 第 3 句
第 1 段 · 第 1 句
第 4 段 · 第 2 句
points: 西班牙征服者前往秘鲁是为了寻找黄金，只是在那里第一次遇到马铃薯。
高产的 potato “crops”是解决方案，填 crops.
clauses: The potato was first cultivated in South America between three and seven thousand years ago, ….
连接词 though 引出“though scientists believe they may have grown wild in the region as long as 13,000 years ago”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 though 把这一层关系补进去。
The genetic patterns of potato distribution indicate ….
“that the potato probably originated in the mountainous west-central region of the continent”补足 indicate 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 indicate 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Jeff Chapman relates the story of history’s most important vegetable
Jeff Chapman 讲述了历史中最重要的蔬菜的故事
